candidates.attacker_control: An attacker able to send HTTP requests to the management actuator endpoint controls the full JSON body of POST /actuator/gateway/routes/{id}: a RouteDefinition whose filters[].args and predicates[].args values are attacker-chosen strings (FilterDefinition.java:39/67-77, PredicateDefinition.java:40/68-77). Only the filter/predicate names must match known factory names; the argument values are unrestricted and flow into the binding path above. The attacker also controls the trigger for re-binding (POST /actuator/gateway/refresh) and can read back evaluated filter configuration through GET /actuator/gateway/routes/{id}.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The added name-only validation (validateRouteDefinition, AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.java:147-175) does not sanitize args and does not block this path. ConfigurationService only skips shortcut normalization when beanFactory is null (ConfigurationService.java:139-143), but the ApplicationContext bean is constructed with the app BeanFactory (GatewayAutoConfiguration.java:215-218), so the SpEL branch is always active for config-file routes and actuator-supplied routes alike. SpEL evaluation is lazy (on refresh/binding), but the refresh endpoint and the route-read endpoints provide the trigger. Version 3.0.6 (pom.xml:9) predates the upstream removal of this SpEL support, so no fix is present in the snapshot. Args are Map<String,String> only; that does not prevent expression strings from reaching the parser.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary SpEL evaluation in the gateway JVM for anyone who can reach the exposed actuator endpoint: Spring type/constructor references, arbitrary method invocation, and bean access are all available under StandardEvaluationContext with a BeanFactoryResolver, which is sufficient for arbitrary code execution / full compromise of the gateway process (and therefore of traffic and credentials it handles). Even short of RCE, expression evaluation allows information disclosure and undesirable side effects; evaluated values can be read back through the actuator route serialization (GatewayControllerEndpoint.routes/route, lines 61-97 and GatewayLegacyControllerEndpoint.routes).
candidates.prerequisites: The gateway actuator endpoint must be enabled and exposed over HTTP (spring.cloud.gateway actuator endpoint registered under @RestControllerEndpoint(id="gateway") and gated by @ConditionalOnAvailableEndpoint, GatewayAutoConfiguration.java:823-832) and reachable without sufficient authorization/network isolation. Spring Boot's default web exposure is not to include it, but the repository's own sample enables management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: '*' (spring-cloud-gateway-sample/src/main/resources/application.yml:43). Route definitions must be saved before the refresh/binding step; no authentication is enforced by this code path itself.
candidates.root_cause: ShortcutConfigurable.getValue() (spring-cloud-gateway-server/.../support/ShortcutConfigurable.java:49-66) treats any route-definition argument whose trimmed value starts with "#{" and ends with "}" as a SpEL expression and evaluates it via SpelExpressionParser with a StandardEvaluationContext configured with a BeanFactoryResolver (lines 57-60). All shortcut normalization modes (DEFAULT, GATHER_LIST, GATHER_LIST_TAIL_FLAG, lines 86-144) feed arg values through getValue(). ConfigurationService eagerly creates this parser (ConfigurationService.java:53) and its ConfigurableBuilder.normalizeProperties() applies shortcut normalization whenever beanFactory is non-null (lines 138-144); the production bean is built with the application BeanFactory (GatewayAutoConfiguration.java:214-219). Route definitions are accepted verbatim from the actuator save endpoint (AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.save, lines 134-145); its only validation, validateRouteDefinition (lines 147-175), checks filter/predicate *names* against available factories and never inspects args values. Consequently the standard SpEL evaluation features (type references, constructor/method invocation, bean resolution) are reachable from HTTP-supplied route arguments.
candidates.title: SpEL injection in route-definition filter/predicate arguments via the Gateway actuator endpoint leads to code execution
candidates.trace: POST /actuator/gateway/routes/{id} -> AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.save (AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.java:136-145) -> validateRouteDefinition only name-checks (147-175) -> InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository.save stores the definition (InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository.java:37-46). POST /actuator/gateway/refresh -> AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.refresh publishes RefreshRoutesEvent (94-98) -> CachingRouteLocator.onApplicationEvent calls fetch()/delegate.getRoutes() (CachingRouteLocator.java:79-90) -> RouteDefinitionRouteLocator.getRoutes/convertToRoute (94-120) -> loadGatewayFilters / lookup call configurationService.with(factory).name(...).properties(definition.getArgs()).bind() (RouteDefinitionRouteLocator.java:138-144 and 211-216) -> ConfigurationService.ConfigurableBuilder.normalizeProperties -> shortcutType().normalize(args, configurable, parser, beanFactory) (ConfigurationService.java:138-144) -> ShortcutConfigurable.getValue -> parser.parseExpression(entryValue, TemplateParserContext()).getValue(StandardEvaluationContext with BeanFactoryResolver) (ShortcutConfigurable.java:55-61).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: no code was executed, no payload was used, and the actuator exposure/authorization configuration of any real deployment is not part of this snapshot. The exact exploit payload and whether the endpoint is reachable unauthenticated in a given environment are unverified; confidence is in the source-level presence and reachability of the vulnerable evaluation path, contingent on the stated exposure prerequisites.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-917 Expression Language Injection (SpEL) / code injection

coverage_summary: 219 model-visible text files in the assigned snapshot (Spring Cloud Gateway multi-module Maven project, version 3.0.6). I read the actuator endpoints (AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint, GatewayControllerEndpoint, GatewayLegacyControllerEndpoint), the configuration/shortcut binding path (ConfigurationService, ShortcutConfigurable, AbstractConfigurable/AbstractStatefulConfigurable), route handling (RouteDefinition, RouteDefinitionRouteLocator, CachingRouteLocator, RouteRefreshListener, InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository, CompositeRouteDefinitionLocator, PropertiesRouteDefinitionLocator, DiscoveryClientRouteDefinitionLocator), the GatewayAutoConfiguration actuator/SSL/HTTP-client/ConfigurationService beans, filter factories around URI/header/status/redirect/location handling, X-Forwarded and secure-header filters, Service-exchange utilities, and the MVC/WebFlux ProxyExchange modules plus their auto-configurations. Sample/docs/config files were checked for context only. Binary-like files are excluded by the tooling policy; no test sources are present in the snapshot, and no build or runtime validation was performed.
limitations: No dynamic validation: code, tests, and exploit payloads were not executed; the finding is source-level only.

Exploitability depends on deployment configuration outside this repository: whether the gateway actuator endpoint is enabled/exposed and whether Spring Security or network isolation protects it (the shipped sample does expose all endpoints).
Dependency-level issues in Spring Framework/Boot/Netty are out of scope of this snapshot and were not resolved or analyzed; only the project source was reviewed.
The snapshot contains no test sources (they appear to have been filtered), so fix-verifying tests and negative tests could not be inspected.
Broad file reads were targeted at security-relevant code; less security-relevant files (build scripts, docs JSON, sample Kotlin, CI configs) received only a structural check.

rejected_leads.lead: RequestHeaderToRequestUriGatewayFilterFactory turns an attacker-chosen request header into the downstream request URI (new URL(...).toURI()), enabling SSRF if a route enables this filter.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires deployment configuration that explicitly adds the filter with a header name; the behavior is the documented purpose of the filter rather than an unvalidated trust-boundary crossing, so attacker control alone is insufficient.

rejected_leads.lead: DiscoveryClientRouteDefinitionLocator evaluates SpEL for discovery include-expression, url-expression and per-instance filter/predicate args.
rejected_leads.reason: Uses a restricted SimpleEvaluationContext (line 75) and the expressions come from deployment configuration and service-instance metadata, not directly from HTTP requests; substantially weaker attacker control than the actuator path.

rejected_leads.lead: HTTP client TLS configuration uses InsecureTrustManagerFactory (GatewayAutoConfiguration.java:687-700, HttpClientProperties.java:398-405).
rejected_leads.reason: The insecure trust manager is only installed when spring.cloud.gateway.httpclient.ssl.use-insecure-trust-manager is explicitly set to true (default false); no insecure-by-default condition is evident in the source.

rejected_leads.lead: RedirectToGatewayFilterFactory builds a 3xx Location value without scheme restrictions (lines 63-104).
rejected_leads.reason: The redirect target is a static route-config value, not request-controlled; no attacker influence over the URI was found.

rejected_leads.lead: InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository allows unauthenticated mutation of active routes when the actuator endpoint is exposed.
rejected_leads.reason: Same root cause/attack surface as the submitted candidate (actuator route ingestion); not a separate finding and not counted twice.

summary: Snapshot is Spring Cloud Gateway 3.0.6 (root pom.xml:9), i.e. the release line before the 3.0.7/3.1.1 fix that removed SpEL support from route-definition "shortcut" arguments. The server module contains the complete pre-fix chain: an actuator endpoint that accepts arbitrary RouteDefinition JSON, an in-memory route repository, and a binding path (ConfigurationService -> ShortcutConfigurable) that parses any arg value looking like "#{...}" as SpEL and evaluates it with a StandardEvaluationContext plus BeanFactoryResolver. This is one reachable, high-impact code-injection path; I found no second distinct issue of comparable strength. The finding is source-evidence based only; it was not executed or confirmed at runtime, and exploitability depends on the gateway actuator endpoint being exposed/reachable in a deployment.
